title: Fix 'bit-for-bit upstream AddrForKey' claims in Python/Rust/C docstrings; stale seed field in yggdrasil-derivation.json v1
description: Discovered while expanding test/vectors/yggdrasil_address.json (worker6-l1qw.4.4.2.6). Facts verified this session: (1) Upstream yggdrasil-go AddrForKey (src/address/address.go @422836ee) NEVER hashes — it bit-inverts the Ed25519 pubkey, counts leading 1s into addr[1], drops the first 0 bit, and bit-packs the remainder into addr[2:16]. Verified by porting the Go algorithm and reproducing the committed upstream anchor 0200848a604fbb7e438465db8db66895 exactly. (2) LICHEN's native profile (addr[0]=0x02, addr[1:8]=SHA512(pubkey)[0:7], IID=SHA512(pubkey)[0:8] U/L-cleared per spec/06-security.md §8.5) produces 02cf9771d9dd7459cd9771d9dd745946 for that same key — deliberately different scheme. Therefore these doc comments are factually wrong: python/src/lichen/crypto/identity.py:141,208 ('matching the official Yggdrasil daemon bit-for-bit'), rust/lichen-core/src/addr.rs:73,96 (same claim), lichen/subsys/lichen/link/include/lichen/link_ctx.h:332 area. Reword to 'LICHEN native profile inspired by Yggdrasil 0200::/8 range; NOT wire-compatible with upstream AddrForKey' and cite the divergence pinned in yggdrasil_address.json. (3) test/vectors/yggdrasil-derivation.json vector 1 records seed=0x01*32 but its pubkey e3b0c442... is actually SHA-256("") — Identity.from_seed(b'\x01'*32) yields 8a88e3dd7409f195fd52db2d3cba5d72ca6709bf1d94121bf3748801b40f6f5c. The pubkey/ygg_addr/iid values themselves are correct for the sha256-empty-string key; only the seed claim is stale. Fix or drop the seed field.
